newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - July 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - July 22.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- The Hong Kong Monetary Authority intervened in the currency market in a bid to preempt possible speculation in the Hong Kong dollar.

-- APPLE DAILY -- The health of jailed Chinese dissident Wang Dan is deteriorating and he is suspected of having a brain tumor. Wang and his family have requested authorities to allow him to be hospitalised and are waiting for a reply.

-- The first traffic accident involving the People's Liberation Army Hong Kong garrison took place when an army jeep ran into a private car. It is unknown how the case will be handled, since PLA jeeps do not have third-party insurance.

-- MING PAO -- China's Minister of Public Security said class struggle still exists because there are domestic and overseas forces which want to refute the late Deng Xiaoping's theory of Socialism with Chinese characteristics.
-- WEN WEI PO -- There are 320 million smokers in China, almost 40 percent of the total population. The number of lung cancer patients is increasing by 66,000 annually.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- About 14,000 people will attend the annual meeting of World Bank and the International Monetary Fund to be held in Hong Kong in September. Senior Chinese leaders will meet foreign financial officials during the meeting.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The government refused to provide funds for a senior counsel to lead the defense in a case challenging the validity of the provisional legislature, and the vital court battle may grind to a halt.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- A study revealed that a continued labour shortage in the construction industry could lead to a HK$9.1 billion decline in Hong Kong's gross domestic product.
